implementation_notes: The Scala-specific hazard is implicits and macro-generated code: an unused-looking implicit may be summoned at a distance, and macro expansions mean the source does not contain the reference. `scalac -Wunused` plus `sbt dependencyTree` covers most cases, and `sbt unused` is the dedicated task. For Play/Akka projects, routes files, reflection configuration and `application.conf` entry points make classes live without any reference in source, so the same caveat as Rails applies.
idiom_name: unused class, unused implicit, unused sbt dependency
pitfalls: Implicits found by search are live without a syntactic reference in the class that uses them.
Macro expansions hide both the definition and the use, so static analysis is structurally limited here.
Play's routes file and Akka's actor registry make classes live without any import or `new` in the source.
